plan: Represent adaptation as a pipeline over freshly built copies: scale, substitute, rewrite, validate; never touch the input structures.
Compute a single Fraction scale factor target_yield / recipe yield and apply it to every ingredient quantity, including component and catalog-added ingredients.

Resolve each ingredient with a substitution chain loop: while its name is excluded, pick the best catalog choice (min of (priority, catalog index)), apply quantity_factor/unit/preparation, and repeat on the new name; a per-chain seen-set detects cycles and a global budget bounds runaway addition loops.
Feed catalog-added additional ingredients into the same worklist so they undergo identical exclusion, substitution, and scaling handling (chained adaptation).

Accumulate substitution side effects (wording change pairs, equipment additions/removals, yield factors, warnings) and apply them once: ordered string replacement over instruction lists, deduplicated sorted equipment checked against available_equipment, and quantity compensation by 1/yield_factor to keep the target yield.

Collect every failure into a reasons set without short-circuiting (missing substitution, unavailable equipment, cycles) and return them sorted; on success return the complete adapted recipe with empty reasons, ordered choice IDs, and sorted warnings.
print_original simply returns authored_text unchanged, which combined with strict non-mutation guarantees byte-for-byte original printing after any adaptations.
mechanisms: single Fraction scale factor applied uniformly to all quantities
per-ingredient substitution chain loop with seen-set cycle detection
deterministic choice selection by (priority, catalog index) minimum
worklist queue routing catalog-added ingredients through the same pipeline
deferred application of accumulated wording/equipment/yield side effects
non-short-circuiting reason accumulation returned as a sorted set
global substitution budget guarding infinite addition loops
fresh-copy construction guaranteeing input immutability and exact authored_text printing
